claims.text: The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is equiatomic.
The equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibits a single-phase solid solution.
The effects of individual constituents can be studied using a composition series in which Hf is increased and the other elements are proportionally adjusted.
Changing the elemental percentages will alter the mechanical properties of HfNbTaTiZr.
Changing composition modifies the atomic-size distribution and produces lattice distortion and local atomic strain.
Hf is a larger-atomic-radius constituent whose enrichment increases lattice distortion in HfNbTaTiZr.
Enhanced lattice distortion can pin dislocations.
Dislocation pinning caused by Hf-induced lattice distortion changes yield strength.
Dislocation pinning caused by Hf-induced lattice distortion changes ductility.
Hf enrichment will produce a non-linear increase in yield strength relative to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Hf enrichment may reduce ductility relative to equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property changes depends on the degree of Hf enrichment.
The proposed relationship applies only while the alloy remains within the single-phase solid-solution stability region.
Compositions outside the single-phase stability region may form secondary phases.
Secondary phases may dominate the mechanical behavior outside the single-phase region.
Consistent tensile testing across the composition series can measure changes in strength and ductility.
X-ray diffraction, lattice-parameter measurements, and electron microscopy can be used to assess phase stability and microstructural changes across the composition series.
